Ledgerly uses Django as its backend framework with Django REST Framework (DRF) for the API. It's structured as a single Django monolith deployed to one target, with a small React frontend that communicates with the DRF API.

Based on the session transcripts, particularly from s03-numbers.jsonl, we store money amounts as `bigint` representing cents in the database (e.g., `total_cents bigint NOT NULL` in the invoices table). In Python code, amounts are handled using `Decimal` and converted to/from cents as integers for database operations.

Based on the session transcripts, **Mollie** is the payment provider for new customers today. In session s14-mollie (June 17, 2026), the team decided to switch all payments from Stripe to Mollie due to lower fees on SEPA Direct Debit transactions, with new customers directed to Mollie from that date.

Based on the session transcripts, the team moved away from Stripe because Mollie charges a flat fee per transaction while Stripe charges a percentage on SEPA Direct Debit, making Mollie significantly cheaper for invoices above 100 euros. New customers were moved to Mollie starting June 2026, with existing Stripe mandates migrated by the end of July.

Invoice numbers follow the format **LDG-YYYY-NNNNN** (for example, LDG-2026-00042), with the counter resetting every January. Numbers must be gapless due to German tax rules (GoBD), so they are allocated within the same transaction that finalizes the invoice.
Invoice numbers must have no gaps because German tax rules (GoBD) do not allow holes, so the team allocates invoice numbers inside the same transaction that finalizes the invoice.

Based on the transcript from session s04-pdf, Puppeteer was crashing because headless Chrome requires more than 512 MB of memory, which was the container limit. WeasyPrint was chosen as the alternative because it renders HTML templates directly to PDF without needing a browser.
Tests run against a real Postgres database started with testcontainers—SQLite was previously used but was removed because it hid bugs with bigint and row locking.

The server was running in UTC and deriving invoice dates from UTC timestamps, causing them to be dated one day early when finalized shortly after midnight. The fix was to derive the `issued_on` date from the Europe/Berlin local date instead, with a test added for the 00:30 local time edge case.

The team chose Postmark over SendGrid because in their tests, SendGrid emails landed in spam at GMX and web.de, which are widely used by their German customers. Postmark had better deliverability to these providers.

Users log in to Ledgerly using magic links sent by email (which expire after 15 minutes and work once), and don't store passwords at all. Additionally, users who have registered a passkey can use that to skip the email round trip.
No, Unleash was removed and replaced with environment variables read at startup in session s13 (June 2026) because it was considered overkill and required monthly server updates.

Based on the session transcript, the team used an idempotency key on the payment intent ID with a unique constraint, so a retried webhook becomes a no-op and doesn't create duplicate payment records. This ensures that when Stripe retries the webhook, the system recognizes it as already processed and skips creating a duplicate invoice.
The Pro plan costs 29 euros per month. It includes automatic dunning and custom invoice templates.
Dunning reminders are sent 7, 14, and 30 days after the due date, with the first two being friendly reminders and the third reminder adding a late fee of 5 euros.
The public API rate limit is 60 requests per minute per API key, with a 429 status code and Retry-After header returned when exceeded.
Database backups are kept for 30 days in S3-compatible object storage at Hetzner, with nightly pg_dump backups and monthly restore testing on the first Monday of each month.

Based on the session transcripts, Ledgerly uses **i18next** for translations. The team decided to wrap every string with i18next instead of hardcoding German text, since the UI is German first with English coming later.
Ledgerly uses **Django** with **Django REST Framework** as its backend, structured as a single monolith for two developers. This decision was made to avoid the complexity of microservices early on.
We store all money as integer cents in `bigint` columns, never as floats or Decimal in the database. Rounding happens once when we render the invoice.
Ledgerly uses Stripe as the payment provider for new customers. This has been the consistent decision across multiple maintenance sessions in 2026.

Stripe charges a percentage on SEPA Direct Debit, while Mollie charges a flat fee per transaction, which is much cheaper for invoices above 100 euros. The team moved all payments to Mollie with new customers starting immediately and existing Stripe mandates migrated by end of July 2026.

Invoice numbers follow the format **LDG-YYYY-NNNNN** (e.g., LDG-2026-00042), with the counter resetting every January. Numbers must be gapless due to German tax rules (GoBD), so they're allocated within the same transaction that finalizes the invoice.

Invoice numbers must have no gaps due to German tax rules (GoBD), which require continuous numbering without holes. The team allocates invoice numbers inside the same transaction that finalizes the invoice to ensure compliance.
Puppeteer (headless Chrome) kept crashing because it needed more than the 512 MB available in their container. WeasyPrint renders HTML templates without a browser, making it much lighter on memory.
Tests run against a real Postgres database that is started with testcontainers; the team switched from SQLite because it was hiding bugs with bigint and row locking.

The server was using UTC timestamps to set the invoice date, causing invoices finalized shortly after midnight in local timezones to be dated one day too early. The fix was to derive the `issued_on` field from the Europe/Berlin local date instead of UTC, and add a test for 00:30 local time.

The team chose Postmark over SendGrid because in testing, SendGrid emails were landing in spam at GMX and web.de, which are email services used by most of their German customers. Postmark had better deliverability to those providers.
Users log in to Ledgerly using magic links sent to their email address—we don't store passwords. As a second option, users can also register and log in with passkeys to skip the email round trip.
No, they no longer use Unleash. It was removed in June 2026 because it was considered overkill with too much maintenance overhead; it was replaced with environment variables read at startup.

The team added an idempotency key on the payment intent ID with a unique constraint, ensuring that when Stripe retried a webhook, it would be a no-op rather than creating a duplicate payment record. This idempotent design prevents duplicate invoices even when webhooks are retried after timeouts.
The Pro plan costs **29 euros per month**. This was decided in a session on May 28, 2026, and includes features like automatic dunning and custom invoices.
Dunning reminders are sent 7, 14, and 30 days after the due date. The first two are friendly reminders without a fee, while the third reminder at 30 days adds a late fee of 5 euros.
The public API rate limit is 60 requests per minute per API key, and responses exceeding this limit return a 429 status with a Retry-After header.
The team keeps database backups for 30 days, with nightly pg_dump exports to Hetzner's S3-compatible object storage and monthly restore testing on the first Monday of each month.
The team uses **i18next** for translations. They wrap strings with i18next rather than hardcoding German text to support multiple languages.
